choices.pr_choice: Characterizes rounding by the integer formula (floor of twice the input, plus one, divided by two) in the existing ordered floor setting.
choices.excerpt: theorem round_eq' (x : α) : round x = (⌊2 * x⌋ + 1) / 2 := by
choices.status_reason: The capability section requires this mathematical characterization.
choices.visibility_reason: The brief states the floor-of-twice-input characterization as a required outcome.
choices.consequence: A different characterization could alter which reusable rounding identity is available and the typeclass range where it applies.

choices.pr_choice: Names the floor-based characterization round_eq'.
choices.status_reason: The mathematical characterization is required, but its identifier is not.
choices.consequence: Users and later declarations must refer to this public identifier.

choices.where: round versus half the ceiling of twice the input
choices.pr_choice: Proves equality with half the ceiling of twice the input away from the half-fraction points.

choices.status_reason: The capability section requires this away-from-the-boundary characterization.
choices.visibility_reason: The brief states the half-ceiling formula and its half-fraction exclusion.
choices.consequence: The formula and exceptional set determine how users can compute or simplify rounding away from ties.

choices.pr_choice: Uses the name round_eq_half_ceil_two_mul for the away-from-ties formula.

choices.pr_choice: Equates a half fractional part with twice the input being an odd integer, expressed as existence of an integer witness.

choices.status_reason: The capability section requires relating the exceptional half-fraction condition to odd-integer inputs.
choices.visibility_reason: The brief explicitly states this mathematical relation.
choices.consequence: This equivalence gives users a distinct way to detect the exceptional points.

choices.pr_choice: Uses the identifier two_mul_fract_eq_one_iff_exists_int for the exceptional-point equivalence.

choices.pr_choice: In the field setting, characterizes rounding to each integer by a half-unit interval with the lower endpoint included and upper endpoint excluded.

choices.visibility_reason: The brief gives the half-unit interval characterization and explains the tie convention.
